questions.prompt: x = [-2, 0.5, 3] and dout = [1, 1, 1]. What does relu_backward(dout, x) return?
questions.explanation: ReLU gates the upstream gradient: it passes where x > 0 and is zeroed elsewhere, giving [0, 1, 1].

questions.prompt: Why subtract max(x) before exponentiating in softmax?
options: It makes the output sum to 1
It prevents overflow without changing the result
It's required for the axis argument to work
questions.explanation: Softmax is invariant to shifting all logits, so subtracting the max keeps every exponent ≤ 0 and nothing overflows.

questions.prompt: Why do networks need non-linear activations at all?
options: Without them, stacked layers collapse to a single linear map
questions.explanation: W₂(W₁x) = (W₂W₁)x. Without a non-linearity between layers, depth adds no expressive power.
